lines.text: But both sets of people, those who are entirely absorbed in
their work and for whom Sunday is merely a day of outward
relaxation, and the others who are indifferent to their work,
and who misuse Sunday in chasing the pleasures of the world,
are not always to be so clearly separated. Many men, in
fact most, have something of both attitudes in themselves
and sometimes behave in one way, sometimes in the other.
Not one of us does not stand in danger of misusing Sunday
and forgetting that it is the Lord's Day whose yoke we should
take upon us and from whom we should learn.
There were once times, and even to-day there are still
many places, where the Sabbath rest was most strictly carried
out and where any kind of amusement or pleasure on Sunday
was considered an abuse. The danger often is indeed that
the easy yoke of the Lord may become oppressive; in which
case the freedom for which it is the purpose of this day to
liberate us, turns into a form of slavery. But for the majority
of us, generally speaking, this danger is not great; on the
contrary! And we should do our best to maintain sound and
ancient Sunday customs. The latter of course seem harsh and
oppressive to those who have not grasped the true meaning
of Sunday. And the chief point is that we should keep alive
the sense of this meaning and purpose among our people,
or revive it if need be; that we should try to instil an under-
standing of the truth that our life should not be wholly
taken up in preoccupation with the things of time and space,
whether it be a question of work or pleasure; that our souls
belong to a higher world, to God's world. Then even Sunday
customs which formerly perhaps may have seemed harsh and
enslaving, will become a light burden and we shall be
grateful to them because they have disciplined us and
enabled us to taste to the full the healing blessings of Sunday.
If anyone should ask whether it is at all permissible for us
to enjoy games and innocent pleasures on Sunday, we
would feel inclined to ask him: what after all is true earthly
enjoyment? "The earth is the Lord's and the fullness
thereof!" We may surely enjoy what the Lord's earth gives
